title: Brennan2019: EEG during Naturalistic Listening to Alice in Wonderland
description: Scalp EEG recorded from participants listening to a 12.4-minute audiobook recording of the first chapter of Alice's Adventures in Wonderland. The naturalistic paradigm was designed to study how the brain builds hierarchical syntactic structure and makes rapid, incremental linguistic predictions. Per-word events are annotated with lexical frequency, sound power, and n-gram, RNN and context-free-grammar surprisal predictors. Behavioral comprehension scores are included for each participant.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with a 61-channel equidistant easyCAP M10 montage and a BrainVision actiCHamp amplifier at 500 Hz, with an online filter of 0.01-200 Hz. Of these channels, 60 scalp channels were retained, together with a vertical EOG channel and an audio channel carrying the stimulus. The audiobook was divided into 12 segments and presented through insert earphones at 45 dB above each participant's hearing threshold. Participants then answered multiple-choice comprehension questions. Data were collected between March 2015 and December 2016 at the University of Michigan.
